decisions.reason: Despite its absence from recent website observations, transactional email is a strategic core extension of the firm's cloud messaging platform and is more likely to be retained or absorbed into a broader offer than discontinued.

Document capture and recognition still fits the firm's push into digital document workflows for regulated customers, though the lack of recent visibility raises some risk of reprioritization or bundling.
Email and fax conversion remains useful for customers bridging legacy and digital channels, but its modest profile and transitional character make it materially more exposed to rationalization.
A narrow fax optimization feature is the most likely candidate to be folded into the core platform or removed as the firm concentrates resources on broader cloud messaging innovations.
Threat sandboxing directly supports the firm's secure-communications positioning and should remain valuable, even if it is increasingly packaged as part of a wider security stack.
Multi-engine virus scanning is relevant but close to standard baseline email security, so it is a plausible product to retire as a distinct offer in favor of integrated security capabilities.
